Chapter 3: Accepting the Worst and Building Upward from There
You know, one of the most powerful ways to break free from worry is to face the worst-case scenario head-on. It sounds intimidating at first, but this mindset can actually be a real game changer. The idea is simple—there are three main steps: accept that the worst could happen, get ready to deal with it if it does, and then focus your energy on making things better.
This isn’t about being negative or expecting disaster. It’s actually about freeing yourself from the grip of fear, so you can think more clearly.
Let me give you an example. Imagine you’re a business owner, and you’re worried about a big financial loss. The first thing to do? Take a moment and calmly spell out what the absolute worst outcome could be. Maybe it’s losing your investment.
Next, you prepare yourself—both in your mind and in practical ways—for the possibility that this might actually happen. What would you do if it did? How would you cope?
Once you’ve faced that, something surprising happens. The fear of the unknown starts to fade. Suddenly, you can put your energy into finding solutions—maybe you can prevent the loss, or at least soften the blow.
So, if we break it down, here’s the method:
First, get crystal clear about what the worst possible outcome really is.
Then, accept—at least in your mind—that it could happen.
Next, prepare yourself to handle it, just in case.
And finally, once fear is no longer running the show, focus your efforts on making things better.
When you accept the worst, your mind stops fighting or denying it. There’s finally room to think creatively, and your motivation can kick back in.
Here’s the thing—most of the time, the worst doesn’t actually happen. But when you face it directly, it loses its power to make you anxious.
That’s how you turn fear into action, and start building upward from wherever you are.
